region.name: Phoenix Metro

origin.label: Central & Washington
origin.note: Phoenix addresses count outward from Central Ave and Washington St on a one-mile arterial grid.
origin.eastHint: East of Central, numbered roads are STREETS (e.g. 24th St). "Ave vs St" instantly tells you which side of Central you're on.
origin.westHint: West of Central, numbered roads are AVENUES (e.g. 19th Ave). "Ave vs St" instantly tells you which side of Central you're on.

region.intro: Every address is measured from Central Ave (east/west) and Washington St (north/south). Arterials fall on a one-mile grid — learn ~10 of them and you can place almost any address.

corridors.name: I-10
corridors.desc: The east–west interstate. Papago Freeway west of downtown (runs under Margaret T. Hance Park in the Deck Park Tunnel), then the Maricopa Freeway bending south past Sky Harbor through the Broadway Curve toward Tempe and Chandler.

corridors.name: I-17
corridors.desc: Black Canyon Freeway — the west-side north–south spine. Meets I-10 twice: at the Stack (west of downtown) and at the Split (south of downtown).

corridors.name: SR 51
corridors.desc: Piestewa Freeway — the north–south express route from the Mini-Stack (I-10/Loop 202) up past Piestewa Peak to Loop 101 in north Phoenix.

corridors.name: Loop 101
corridors.desc: The outer ring: Agua Fria Freeway on the west side, Pima Freeway across the north and down Scottsdale, Price Freeway through Tempe/Chandler.

corridors.name: Loop 202
corridors.desc: Red Mountain Freeway east from the Mini-Stack along the Salt River; the South Mountain segment closes the loop around the far side of South Mountain.

corridors.name: US 60
corridors.desc: Superstition Freeway — leaves I-10 at the Broadway Curve and carries East Valley commuters through Tempe and Mesa.

corridors.name: SR 143
corridors.desc: Hohokam Expressway — a short connector along the east edge of Sky Harbor linking I-10 to Loop 202.

corridors.name: Grand Ave
corridors.desc: The only major diagonal in the grid. Follows the BNSF railroad northwest from downtown toward Glendale, Peoria and Wickenburg — and creates notorious six-way intersections where it crosses the grid.

corridors.name: Bell Rd
corridors.desc: Northern commercial strip, roughly 13 miles north of Washington St. One of the longest continuous arterials in the Valley — runs from Surprise to Scottsdale.

corridors.name: Thunderbird Rd
corridors.desc: 11 miles north. Crosses I-17 and SR 51; marks the north edge of Sunnyslope / Moon Valley territory.

corridors.name: Northern Ave
corridors.desc: 7 miles north. A key west-side crosstown route through Glendale; east of SR 51 it becomes the edge of Paradise Valley (the town).

corridors.name: Glendale Ave
corridors.desc: 6 miles north. Runs into downtown Glendale on the west; east of 16th St it turns into Lincoln Drive, the scenic route between the mountains.

corridors.name: Camelback Rd
corridors.desc: 4 miles north. The Valley's premier east–west business corridor — Biltmore, Arcadia, and Scottsdale Fashion Square all sit on it.

corridors.name: Indian School Rd
corridors.desc: 3 miles north. Links Maryvale to Old Town Scottsdale; light-rail-adjacent at Central.

corridors.name: Thomas Rd
corridors.desc: 2 miles north. Hospital corridor (Banner, St. Joseph's nearby) and the north edge of Papago Park.

corridors.name: McDowell Rd
corridors.desc: 1 mile north. The traditional north edge of downtown; continues east past the Phoenix Zoo into Scottsdale.

corridors.name: Van Buren St
corridors.desc: Downtown's northern east–west street, a few blocks north of Washington. Historic US 80 corridor toward Tolleson.

corridors.name: Washington St
corridors.desc: The north/south ZERO LINE of the address grid. Every "N" or "S" address is measured from here. Light rail runs along it east of downtown to Sky Harbor.

corridors.name: Buckeye Rd
corridors.desc: 1 mile south. Freight and airport-industrial corridor along the north edge of Sky Harbor.

corridors.name: Broadway Rd
corridors.desc: 2 miles south. Runs into Tempe just south of ASU; gives its name to the I-10 "Broadway Curve".

corridors.name: Southern Ave
corridors.desc: 3 miles south. South Phoenix's main crosstown and a long East Valley arterial through Tempe and Mesa.

corridors.name: Baseline Rd
corridors.desc: 4 miles south. Literally the survey baseline for all Arizona land surveys; skirts the north foot of South Mountain.

corridors.name: 67th Ave
corridors.desc: West-side boundary road between Phoenix (Maryvale) and Glendale; crosses I-10 near Desert Sky Mall.

corridors.name: 51st Ave
corridors.desc: Maryvale's central north–south arterial; south of I-10 it serves the industrial southwest.

corridors.name: 43rd Ave
corridors.desc: West-side arterial running the full length of the city, Baseline to the Loop 101.

corridors.name: 35th Ave
corridors.desc: Crosses Grand Ave and I-17 area; long continuous route from South Mountain to north Phoenix.

corridors.name: 19th Ave
corridors.desc: One mile west of Central. The light rail turns onto 19th Ave north of Camelback toward Metro Center.

corridors.name: 7th Ave
corridors.desc: Half-mile west of Central. Reversible-lane commuter route into downtown during rush hour.

corridors.name: Central Ave
corridors.desc: The east/west ZERO LINE of the address grid: west of here streets are "Avenues", east of here they are "Streets". Light rail runs along it through Midtown.

corridors.name: 7th St
corridors.desc: Half-mile east of Central. Mirror of 7th Ave, with its own reversible lanes; runs past Chase Field.

corridors.name: 16th St
corridors.desc: One mile east of Central. Spine of the Calle 16 murals district and a back door to Sky Harbor's west side.

corridors.name: 24th St
corridors.desc: 1.5 miles east. Direct access to Sky Harbor's west terminal side and the heart of the Biltmore at Camelback.

corridors.name: 32nd St
corridors.desc: 2 miles east. Runs along the Biltmore's east edge and over the Phoenix Mountains Preserve gap.

corridors.name: 44th St
corridors.desc: East-side link from Sky Harbor (east entrance) north to Camelback; western boundary of Arcadia.

corridors.name: Scottsdale / Rural Rd
corridors.desc: One continuous line with two names: Scottsdale Road north of the Salt River, Rural Road through ASU and Tempe to the south.

corridors.name: Hayden Rd
corridors.desc: Scottsdale's second north–south spine, following the Indian Bend Wash greenbelt.

districts.name: Downtown Phoenix
districts.why: Government, sports, and convention core. Every grid number starts counting here.

districts.name: Midtown
districts.why: High-rise office corridor along Central Ave and light rail, between downtown and Uptown.

districts.name: Encanto
districts.why: Historic district around Encanto Park, west of Midtown.

districts.name: Uptown / North Central
districts.why: Leafy residential spine along Central and 7th St; the Uptown Plaza and Melrose district.

districts.name: Biltmore / Camelback Corridor
districts.why: The Valley's premium office market, anchored by 24th St & Camelback.

districts.name: Arcadia
districts.why: Citrus-grove neighborhood at the foot of Camelback Mountain, between Phoenix and Scottsdale.

districts.name: Sky Harbor Center
districts.why: The airport and its logistics belt — reached via I-10, SR 143, Loop 202 or 24th/44th St.

districts.name: Eastlake / Coronado
districts.why: Historic neighborhoods just east of downtown, cut by the I-10 / SR 51 interchange.

districts.name: Papago Park / Zoo
districts.why: Buttes, the Phoenix Zoo and Desert Botanical Garden — the green gap between Phoenix, Tempe and Scottsdale.

districts.name: Downtown Tempe / ASU
districts.why: ASU main campus and Mill Ave on the south shore of Tempe Town Lake.

districts.name: Old Town Scottsdale
districts.why: Scottsdale's walkable core: galleries, nightlife and Fashion Square.

districts.name: South Phoenix
districts.why: Historic agricultural belt between the Salt River and South Mountain.

districts.name: Alhambra
districts.why: West-central Phoenix along I-17 and Grand Ave; home to Grand Canyon University.

districts.name: Maryvale
districts.why: Phoenix's first master-planned suburb (1950s), on the west side.

districts.name: Sunnyslope
districts.why: Hillside neighborhood tucked under North Mountain, between I-17 and SR 51.
